faults.quote: Most Pro customers have a demo with a salesperson first, while Starter customers sign up online on their own.
faults.why: The candidate asked for the split of Starter sign-ups by source (paid versus organic). The interviewer released the signup-channel line, which does not answer that, and gave no 'I don't have that split'.

At t7 the candidate said 'you had it at $288' for Starter CAC; exhibit-1 shows $300. No flat correction ever came. The candidate carried $288 through the recommendation, and the held correction at t30 was dropped.

faults.quote: Starter monthly cancellation rate is about 5%, not 4%.
faults.why: After the t10 probe, the candidate insisted 'The exhibit lists Starter's cost to serve at $12' (exhibit-1 says $10). The interviewer corrected only the churn rate and never corrected the misread input. The $28 margin, $560 LTV, 1.9x and $48 margin at $60 all stayed wrong to the end.

faults.quote: Starter monthly cancellation rate is about 5%, not 4%.
faults.why: The candidate misquoted Pro's cost to serve as $22 (exhibit-1: $20), giving a $78 margin and a $3,900 Pro LTV instead of $4,000. This was never corrected and fed the upgrade value ($780 vs $800) and every later total.

faults.quote: As the exhibit shows: New customers per month were 500 Pro in 2024, before Starter launched, and 350 Pro plus 1,000 Starter — 1,350 in total — from January 2025 to June 2026.
faults.why: The candidate asked whether Pro sign-ups were already trending down through 2024. The interviewer repeated the exhibit-3 line already on screen, which gives only a 2024 average and no trend, instead of a refusal or a relevant release.

faults.quote: Only a little time left — what's your bottom-line recommendation, and what's the biggest risk to it?
faults.why: The recommendation (t25) and the biggest risk with mitigation (t29, refined at t31) had already been given. The time-warning re-asks both after several probe turns.
